premise: A big pitch at nine tonight: how brands get closer to people over the next ten years. Hit nine sites across Xinyi District and earn one pitch page at each.

prologue.text: [Good morning] Being safe is a blessing. Wear a jacket when you go out.
The breakfast griddle below beats any alarm. Scooter stalled again. Third kick did it.
The usual? Egg crepe with chili, milk tea, no ice. I'll call you when it's ready.
Pitch at nine tonight. Topic: over the next ten years, how do brands get closer to people?
Saw it. Nine sites today, right? Send me a page after each one. I'll lay it out.
Heard you got this pitch too? See you tonight. I'm not going easy on you this time.
A pitch, huh? Extra egg in your crepe, on me. You can't fight on an empty stomach.

lines.text: Everyone's here. Pitch is at nine tonight. That doesn't move.
You've seen the brief. What the client wants is ten years of Intelligent Decision.
Zero pages in the deck, I know. Nine sites. Where do I start?
Start at MRT City Hall Station, Manager Wu's billboard job. Crowds thin by nine. Hurry.
Back here at ten. Director Lin wants to check numbers. I'll send the next stops as you go.
Vicky's on the same pitch. If you run into her, don't let her pump you for info.
After each stop, send me whatever you found. I'll build the pages.
Screenshots, photos, audio, all fine. But numbers need a source, or I won't take them.
Got it. One stop, one page. Nine pages by nine.

back.text: Still out running around? Director Lin says back by nine.
I saved you a coffee. Go do your thing.
Send data and I'll lay it out. No data, I'll assume you're still on your scooter.
Quit spacing out at the door. Numbers don't walk into the deck by themselves.
Vicky's out there too. We can't fall behind her.
No one in the meeting room, no deck either. You'll get further out in the field.

cast.blurb: Started the same year as you. Sharp tongue, but always the first to cover for you when things go wrong.
Few words in person. On LINE, mostly “?” and “OK”; types only for orders. Speaks from the heart once a year.
Ex-colleague who jumped to a rival agency. Tonight she's pitching against you.
Has run Sisi South Village Shop for decades. Sends several good-morning images a day.

interludes.slide: Marketing isn't a bet anymore: see it, measure it, fix it

sincere.text: Honestly, you're the first to think it through for me, not rush to sell me ad slots.

interrupt.text: A campaign truck rolls up Shifu Rd. “Please, please, vote for us!” drowns out the rest.

partner.text: Page one's in. Whatever you picked, Manager Wu left smiling. I'll call that a pass.

grandma.text: Good morning! 30% chance of rain today. Is your raincoat under the seat?

replies.text: Leave it on read and ride

interludes.slide: Data shows the surface, not always the truth

sincere.text: Honestly, if you want to know about the store, just ask us at the counter.

interrupt.text: Director Lin sends a single “?”. You know he means page two.

partner.text: Page two's in. I'll roast your call later, but you asked people on site. Beats the report.

grandma.text: Eat a real lunch, not just coffee again. Ama saw your story. Three days, all coffee.

replies.text: Leave it on read for now
Call her: “Ama, I'll go eat soon.”

interludes.slide: Back to your own customers: first-party data and LTV

sincere.text: Six months of pandemic, and you're the first to tell me not to bet it all on traffic.

interrupt.text: Phone rings: “Hi, your chicken-leg bento's at Wun-Zero-Wun. Security won't let me up.”

partner.text: Page three's in. Who cares if Manager Chen's boss smiled? Cookies wait for no one.

grandma.text: Ama orders by phone now! The noodle shop knows I'm a regular. No cilantro, he remembers.

replies.text: Call her over bento; hear about the noodle shop

sincere.text: Twenty years shooting ads, and this is the one I want to show my mom.

interrupt.text: Every phone in the studio shrieks at once: National Alert. Everyone looks. Pandemic text.

partner.text: Page four's in. Wei's face in the set photos is… complicated. What did you two shoot?

grandma.text: Ama can't remember TV ad lines, only the ones about people. Was today's about people?

replies.text: Leave it on read till wrap
Call her: “It's about people. I'll show you.”

interludes.slide: From me to us: let customers pitch in

sincere.text: I want to do the right thing too. I'm just scared nobody will buy it.

interrupt.text: Thunder rolls. An afternoon storm herds Xiangti Avenue's buskers onto the arcade sidewalk.

partner.text: Page five. Green never gets full marks, but nobody's calling her greenwashing… probably.

grandma.text: Rain! The store got three empty bottles for soy sauce refills. Even young folks do it.

replies.text: Call her: “Ama, this belongs in the deck.”

interludes.slide: AI is a good teammate. People still make the call

sincere.text: Honestly, the better AI gets, the more I value the person beside it counting fingers.

partner.text: Page six. I checked: every hand in the deck has five fingers. Good job.

grandma.text: Someone faked your cousin's voice for cash. Ama asked about his childhood dog. He hung up.

replies.text: Call her: “Ama, you're amazing. Teach me that.”

interludes.slide: Everyone uses AI. Core brand values make the difference

sincere.text: If folks like you still walk into these alleys, this block's got a chance.

interrupt.text: “A Maiden's Prayer” plays. Ah-Cheng drops his spatula and dashes out with two trash bags.

partner.text: Page seven. Bring me a chicken cutlet from Linginger Street. That's favor number seven.

grandma.text: Kids came to Sisi South Village for photos. One taught me to go live; I taught her zongzi.

replies.text: Call her: “Ama, I'll watch every stream.”

interludes.slide: Algorithms: efficiency. Brands: what can't be generated

sincere.text: Twenty years in TV. Budget cuts don't scare me. Nobody watching together does.

interrupt.text: A campaign truck crawls along Zhongxiao E. Rd. Its loudspeaker eats her whole sentence.

partner.text: Page eight. Keep TV or not, I back you. The boss will still ask: what about short video?

grandma.text: You're at the TV station? Ama saw your story. I know those jingles better than you do.

replies.text: Leave it on read, meeting soon
Call her: “Ama, sing me a line.”

interludes.slide: AI helps brands understand people. That's real closeness

sincere.text: These nine pages, you earned one site at a time. Honestly, I…

interrupt.text: The elevator doors cut him off. Your phone rings too: delivery's downstairs at A25.

partner.text: All nine are in. But AI made three takes on the last page. Each looks like someone else's.

grandma.text: Ama doesn't get AI, but you met people. Understand people first. Then make your case.

replies.text: Leave it on read, go on stage
Call her: “Ama, this goes on the last page.”

grandmaSlide.title: Last Page: Ama's Words
grandmaSlide.text: Understand people first. Then make your case.

withGrandma.text: Still thinking about it. That last page went up, and the client went dead quiet.
“Understand people first. Then make your case.” Who wrote that?
Ours had nine pages too, but not that one. This drink's for you.
Pitch over? Eaten yet? Ama wants to hear how you told it today.

withoutGrandma.text: Nine pages, beautifully laid out. Just as beautiful as theirs. That's the problem.
Our conclusions were nearly identical. The client says they'll think it over.
I check my phone. Ama wrote all day. Each one got a read receipt and a sticker. That's it.
Kiddo, just reply to Ama when you have a minute.
